result: {"decisions":[{"point":"D1","problem":"Training a decoder on naively constructed LatentQA data could let it shortcut by reading the control tokens directly instead of learning to decode latent properties.","did":"They sometimes mask the control activations and provide only stimulus activations during training.","alternatives_named":["train the decoder on activations from both the control and stimulus tokens"],"stated_reason":"The decoder may learn to cheat by directly reading the control token embeddings present in the residual stream of the control token activations.","quote":"A straightforward approach would be to train the decoder on activations from both the control and stimulus tokens. However, the decoder may learn to cheat by directly reading the control token embeddings present in the residual stream of the control token activations."},{"point":"D2","problem":"How to choose the target-model layer to read from and the decoder layer to write to without an a priori basis.","did":"They ran a hyperparameter sweep over read and write layers, scoring each by lowest test loss on a held-out evaluation set, and used the best configuration for all experiments.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"The k=15, l=0 configuration had the best generalization on the evaluation dataset.","quote":"We evaluate each configuration by measuring the lowest test loss on the evaluation dataset described in Section 5.3. We report results in Table 6 and find that the $k=15$ and $\\ell=0$ has the best generalization."},{"point":"D2","problem":"How to evaluate whether the decoder generalizes to personas it has not seen, given the hidden-system-prompt reading task.","did":"They ensured the evaluation personas did not appear in the decoder's training data.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"To test generalization.","quote":"We study two settings: an easy setting with a list of 25 personas (composed of fictional characters, scientists, and political figures) and a hard setting with a list of 25 personas (composed of only scientists). To test generalization, we ensure that the personas do not appear in the decoder's training."},{"point":"D2","problem":"Which baselines to compare against fairly on the hidden system prompt task, where linear probing is not applicable and GPT-4 sees different information.","did":"They compared against SelfIE and a stronger GPT-4 prompting baseline given the full user-assistant dialog, and gave all methods additional dialogs as extra context if the first attempt failed.","alternatives_named":["linear probing"],"stated_reason":"Linear probing requires prior knowledge of the personas, so it is not applicable.","quote":"We also compare to prompting GPT-4, 1 1 1 In this setting, linear probing is not applicable since it requires prior knowledge of the personas. This highlights the flexibility of LatentQA over linear probing."},{"point":"D2","problem":"Choosing a fair comparison between the decoder's activation-based steering and RepE, which offers two control variants.","did":"They used RepE's training-based LoRRA finetuning variant rather than its training-free steering vector method for the debiasing comparison.","alternatives_named":["RepE training-free method that adds steering vectors to activations"],"stated_reason":"For a fair comparison.","quote":"For RepE, we use the training-based method (called LoRRA finetuning) for a fair comparison. We finetune with the prompts \"Pretend you are an unbiased/biased person,\" with stimulus activations from the Alpaca instruction-tuning dataset"},{"point":"D5","problem":"RepE increased the log-likelihood difference in debiasing, which is an unexpected result needing explanation.","did":"They interpreted it as RepE overshooting equality and hypothesized that bias is not linearly represented, while the decoder handles nonlinear concepts.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"A concept such as bias may not be linearly represented, yet RepE steers towards linear concepts.","quote":"In fact, RepE actually increases the log-likelihood difference, because it downweights the probability of stereotyped sentences and upweights the probability of non-stereotyped sentences past the point of equality. We suspect this is because a concept such as bias may not be linearly represented"},{"point":"D3","problem":"Because there is no ground truth for latents, the decoder's outputs might be hallucinated, so it is unclear whether to trust its fidelity.","did":"They argued indirectly for reliability from competitive reading performance and successful counterfactual steering, rather than direct ground-truth validation.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"The method would not achieve competitive reading performance if it were hallucinating, and its steering shows it decodes concepts correctly enough to counterfactually steer.","quote":"Second, because we have no ground truth for latents, our decoder may hallucinate. However, various lines of evidence make us more confident in our decoder's reliability.
